status: Final packet 31 (G13-convert) gate; registered before any measured run (only a 3-iteration C smoke ran).
question: After CR13/a,b, is synchronous ASS->VTT conversion on the event loop a remaining dominant loop-stall cost?
code_path: stream/router.py subtitles endpoint: ass_to_vtt(_decode_subtitle_text(raw)) runs inline in the async handler; result cached per key; source capped by subtitle_max_source_bytes = 8 MiB.
source_C: frozen aaa9ee5 server/app overlay (g02-post-cr17-v2 manifest re-verified); A/B use the image built-in app; missing converter => N/A.
fixtures: Deterministic synthetic ASS: typical ~120 KB / 1202 dialogue lines (UTF-8 and cp1250 fallback), heavy ~3 MB karaoke/sign typesetting, limit just under 8 MiB. Synthetic, not a claim about every real file.
sampling: 5 repetitions x A/B/C rotated, each a fresh 1-CPU process on cpuset 6 / 1 GiB / network none; per fixture and mode 3 warmup + 20 timed conversions.
metric: Largest gap of a 1 ms asyncio heartbeat during one conversion (loop stall), per-run p95 over 20 conversions; wall and thread CPU time; output sha and cue count.
concurrency_note: Runs alongside G03 (CPU 2-5), G04 (12-14) and possibly the tail of G02 (0,1) on disjoint cpusets.
decision: C inline: NO_CHANGE if every fixture median gap p95 < 10 ms (plan 10 ms piece/normal-HTTP budget); BUDGET_EXCEEDED_NOT_DOMINANT if >= 10 ms but none > 29.016 ms; OFFLOAD_CANDIDATE if some fixture median > 29.016 ms (largest remaining CR13/b post looplag p99-median, 500 fixture) with >= 2 runs above. INVALID on missing C runs, unavailable converter, non-WEBVTT or run-to-run output difference. to_thread results are informative design input only (GIL sharing).
limits: Microbenchmark of the exact production functions under a heartbeat loop, not a full-app looplag profile; the cache means one conversion per file key per process. No code change by this gate.
